digest.component_or_area: dependency advisory CI gating and resolution workflow
propositions: A committed lock freezes transitive dependencies, causing any published advisory against a pinned version to fail the gating pip-audit job on all in-flight changes regardless of whether those changes touch the dependency map

Developers attempting to resolve a transitive-dependency advisory encounter false-progress moves (uv lock --upgrade-package being a no-op against an upstream cap; constraint-dependencies returning UNSATISFIABLE as expected output, not proof of impossibility) that lead to wrong conclusions without documented guidance
The Gerrit verify lane should block on an advisory only when the change touches the dependency map (uv.lock or pyproject dependency declarations), ensuring only the owner of that map owns the defect

The scheduled CI main lane must fail visibly and escalate (file/update a ticket) when an outstanding advisory exists, so releases never ship on a known-vulnerable pin, with deduplication to prevent noise across multiple runs

Documentation must establish that override-dependencies (not constraint-dependencies) is the correct escape hatch when an upstream cap blocks an upgrade, and must require a justification naming the advisory, the capping package, and evidence the override is safe

A runbook covering real-vs-flake triage, the constraint-vs-override distinction, the uv lock --upgrade-package no-op behavior, and the verification set (uv lock --check; uv sync --locked --extra dev; pip-audit full environment scan) must be discoverable from job failure output
